newsitem.title: Israel: Israel's Weizman begins meeting PLO's Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Weizman begins meeting PLO's Arafat.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman went into a meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday in a bid to revive stalled Israel-PLO peace talks, witnesses said.

The two men shook hands and began their meeting on the border between Israel and the Gaza Strip in the face of a seven-week-old freeze in Israel-PLO peacemaking triggered by Israel's settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We don't have a written agenda. First of all the main agenda is to meet and to say 'ahalan wasahalan' (greetings) -- and then to just discuss...how to break the ice," Weizman told reporters. "We haven't seen each other for some time."
Earlier, Weizman said he hoped he and Arafat would find "a way to move the peace process which is stuck in the sand".

Israeli-PLO peace talks were broken off after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave bulldozers the green light in March to break ground for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on land claimed by Israel and the Palestinians.
Palestinians said they would not back down from a demand that the East Jerusalem settlement and settlement building in the West Bank and Gaza Strip be halted.
